tone: majestic yet accessible, worshipful, self-giving, climactic, Christ-centered
target_reader: religion-naive adults and older adolescents near grade 6
translation_identity: firmly dynamic-equivalence, NLT-like in readability but independent

sealed_unit.instruction: The completed human-edited wording of Philippians 2:1-4 is excluded from blind drafting.

governing_rules: The prose serves the reader; the apparatus serves accountability.
Translate meaning, logic, tone, discourse movement, and theological force rather than Greek surface form.
Use clear natural oral English; reorder, split, unpack, and clarify implied relationships when comprehension benefits.
Preserve the passage's movement from Christ's status, through self-humbling and death, to God's exaltation and universal acknowledgment.
Do not turn contested clauses into unsupported commentary; document consequential resolutions as risks or human questions.
No comparison translations, traditional benchmark wording, or sealed human wording may enter blind drafting.
existing_decisions: Use Christ and Jesus Christ naturally according to the source reference.
Maintain the reader-first dynamic center established by the audited Philippians 1 benchmark without exposing its wording to blind workers.

units.title: Christ’s self-humbling and exaltation
known_issues: Verse 5 connects the community's mindset to the mindset embodied by Christ; preserve the ethical bridge from verses 1-4 without exposing their human-edited wording.
Verse 6's μορφῇ θεοῦ affirms divine status or form; avoid reducing it to mere appearance.
Verse 6's ἁρπαγμός is disputed: Christ did not regard equality with God as something to seize, exploit, or use for His own advantage. Any resolution must preserve the contrast with self-giving.
Verse 7's 'emptied Himself' is metaphorical and explained by taking servant form and becoming human; do not imply that Christ ceased to be divine or discarded divine attributes.
μορφή is used for both God and servant in verses 6-7; keep the conceptual relationship accountable even if English wording differs.
δοῦλος carries servant/slave force; choose accessible wording without erasing low status.
Verses 7-8 affirm genuine human existence and radical obedience culminating in the shameful death of a cross.
Verse 9 makes God's exaltation a response to Christ's self-humbling and speaks of the supreme bestowed name; avoid prematurely inserting an unstated name unless clearly documented.
Verses 10-11 have universal cosmic scope: beings in heaven, on earth, and under the earth bow, and every tongue acknowledges Jesus Christ as Lord.
Preserve the climax 'Jesus Christ is Lord' and its result: glory to God the Father.

verses.greek: τοῦτο φρονεῖτε ἐν ὑμῖν ὃ καὶ ἐν Χριστῷ Ἰησοῦ
ὃς ἐν μορφῇ θεοῦ ὑπάρχων οὐχ ἁρπαγμὸν ἡγήσατο τὸ εἶναι ἴσα θεῷ
ἀλλὰ ἑαυτὸν ἐκένωσεν μορφὴν δούλου λαβών ἐν ὁμοιώματι ἀνθρώπων γενόμενος καὶ σχήματι εὑρεθεὶς ὡς ἄνθρωπος
ἐταπείνωσεν ἑαυτὸν γενόμενος ὑπήκοος μέχρι θανάτου θανάτου δὲ σταυροῦ
διὸ καὶ ὁ θεὸς αὐτὸν ὑπερύψωσεν καὶ ἐχαρίσατο αὐτῷ τὸ ὄνομα τὸ ὑπὲρ πᾶν ὄνομα
ἵνα ἐν τῷ ὀνόματι Ἰησοῦ πᾶν γόνυ κάμψῃ ἐπουρανίων καὶ ἐπιγείων καὶ καταχθονίων
καὶ πᾶσα γλῶσσα ἐξομολογήσηται ὅτι κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς εἰς δόξαν θεοῦ πατρός
